claims.text: As-processed HfNbTiVAl10 exhibits a hierarchical heterostructure with multiscale compositional and microstructural modulations.
High-resolution imaging and diffraction can quantify nanoprecipitate size, spacing, and distribution in HfNbTiVAl10.
High-resolution imaging and diffraction can quantify mesoscale grain-boundary and compositional-gradient heterogeneities in HfNbTiVAl10.
A machine-learning model can combine imaging-derived microstructural descriptors with limited tensile and fracture test data.
The model will learn correlations between hierarchical microstructural features and stress-strain behavior.
Capturing multiscale microstructural influences will allow the model to predict Young's modulus.
Capturing multiscale microstructural influences will allow the model to predict yield strength.
Capturing multiscale microstructural influences will allow the model to predict crack initiation and propagation behavior.
The proposed model will predict the specified mechanical responses more accurately than conventional atomistic, continuum, or finite-element simulations.
The proposed model will reduce prediction error by at least 10% relative to conventional simulations.
The proposed model may reduce computation time by an order of magnitude relative to conventional simulations.
Conventional atomistic, continuum, and finite-element simulation techniques are computationally intensive for this prediction task.
Conventional simulations tend to average out critical microstructural heterogeneities.
Averaging out critical microstructural heterogeneities reduces the accuracy of conventional simulations.
The proposed approach is expected to apply across strain rates and potentially across temperatures when the hierarchical microstructure is preserved.
Model performance may fail to improve if the imaging data do not represent the full variability of the hierarchical structure.
Unrepresented phase transformations or severe local damage during testing may cause the model to fail.
Predictions may degrade under extreme loading conditions absent from the training data.

Independent testing will falsify the hypothesis if improvement in prediction error is below 10% or computational speedup is below 5-fold relative to conventional simulations across multiple test cases.
